A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forgetting-based SFT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite pagination changes and the added computational cost section.

before.justification: V4 reports original LLM benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B, including comparisons across model sizes and architectures.

after.justification: V5 retains those original experiments and additionally reports computational cost measurements in Appendix B.6 and Table 11.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, influence-based token scoring, token partitioning and the adaptive forgetting objective in Equation 8 are unchanged. The correction to the background SFT formula does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The five training datasets, five primary evaluation benchmarks and four additional benchmarks in Appendix B.3 are retained. The duplicate-reference-data scenario also already appears in v4.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same base-model, full-token SFT, ignoring and forgetting comparisons, including sequence-level and token-level variants. The added timing analysis uses existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 adds comparative cost accounting for 3B and 8B models, distinguishing training-only time from totals including preprocessing and reporting percentage overhead. Existing task metrics, data splits, training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.6 analyzes where computational overhead arises, separating warmup, influence scoring and training costs. Existing granularity, token-ratio, forgetting-rate, duplicate-data and lambda analyses are retained; Table 10 is relocated, not new.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 6 retain means and standard deviations from three independent training runs. V5 adds no repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedures; the new timing table reports point values.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds runtime results: total forgetting time is 270 versus 205 minutes for full-token training at 3B, and 436 versus 347 minutes at 8B, with reported overheads of 31.71% and 25.65%. Existing benchmark and ablation values in Tables 3–10 and Figure 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 replaces normalization by an unexplained sum of w_i,j with division by the token-index count |I|, correcting the background SFT loss definition. The remaining mathematics is unchanged, with no new assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the claim of improving diversity, and the abstract and conclusion remove assertions about forming clearer knowledge boundaries. The central claim that explicit forgetting improves SFT performance and generalization is retained.

C2.justification: Knowledge-boundary explanations are removed while the existing regularization and capacity explanations remain. Appendix B.6 newly argues that computational overhead is justified and preprocessing can be reused across runs; Section 6's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: V4's approximate model-training times are retained and supplemented with component-level and total timings in Table 11. Hardware, software versions, LoRA settings, optimizer and other training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 drops v4's separate citation and reference for 'Unlearning with control' (reference 51). The broader positioning against data selection, unlearning and preference optimization remains stable; duplicated Chung et al. entries are consolidated, and most other bibliography edits concern metadata.

P1.justification: V5 makes localized grammar and explanation edits, updates authorship and correspondence information, revises bibliographic entries and adds Appendix B.6. The overall section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V5 adds Table 11 and relocates existing material, including Tables 1 and 10, with accompanying text and reference reflow. Existing table designs and Figure 1's plots, axes, legends and values are retained.

improvement.justification: V5 corrects Equation 1, supplements rough training-time estimates with explicit computational cost accounting, and narrows diversity and knowledge-boundary claims. These improve precision and transparency without materially expanding empirical validation. The assertion that preprocessing can be ignored across repeated runs remains insufficiently qualified, but the reported totals still provide a useful, limited quality improvement.
